function.name: Music_3_LookupMusic
function.description: Finds songs that align with the user's musical preferences based on the artist, album, genre, and release year. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

artist.description: The name of the artist performing the song. Use 'dontcare' to ignore this criterion.

album.description: The name of the album that the song is part of. Use 'dontcare' to ignore this criterion.

genre.description: The genre of the music. Use 'dontcare' to indicate no specific preference.

year.description: The year of the song's initial release. Format should be a four-digit number, e.g., '2001'. Use 'dontcare' to ignore this criterion.

message.content: I don’t have direct access to your listening history, so I can’t automatically pull up the tracks you’ve played most this week. If you can tell me a bit about those songs—such as the artist, album, genre, or release year—I can search for similar tracks that match those details. Let me know what you’d like to focus on!
message.reasoning: The user wants to find songs they've played the most this week. We need to use the Music_3_LookupMusic function? But that function finds songs based on artist, album, genre, year. It doesn't accept "most played this week". There's no function to get play history. The user wants songs they've played the most this week. We don't have a function for that. We can ask clarifying question: "Do you want me to search your library for songs that match your most played songs this week?" But we can't retrieve that data. We might respond that we don't have that capability. Or we can ask for more info. The user specifically: "Please find me any of the songs that I've played the most this week." We could interpret that as they want to find songs that match their most played songs. But we don't have data. We can ask them to provide the list of songs or the artist/album. Alternatively, we can ask them to specify criteria. The best approach: explain that we don't have access to play history, but we can help find songs based on artist, album, genre, year. Ask for details.
